messages:
maya: Heads up — we're seeing a sustained increase in 5xx and tail p99 timeouts for hosted inference. Alerts started ~10m ago for tenant acme-inc. Gateway logs show repeated request queue depth hits and continuous-batcher backlog. https://grafana.redwood.example/d/queue?s=now-30m
josh: oncall here, looking. Which gateway/region? any tenant rate changes? @tom can you pull batcher metrics?
maya: hosted-us-east gateway. tenant acme-inc traffic spiked ~3x around 10:12. queue_depth at 100% on several hosts, dequeue lag growing. p95 latency up ~600ms, p99 > 5s, and a bunch of 502/504 spikes.
priya: support case CS-9241 opened by AE earlier for auth errors — possibly related? Customer says they retried a lot.
tom: grabbing logs now. infra-bot: metric snapshot attached -> batcher_pending=18k, dequeue_rate=250/s, batch_window_ms=25, avg_batch_size=9
josh: that pending number is huge. Could be continuous batching KV cache pressure + slow model runtime. Any long sequences causing big KV spikes?
maya: yes, many long seq requests from that tenant (avg tokens 1200). kvcache hit ratio fell to 0.4 and evictions spiked.
ops-oncall: recommended immediate mitigations: 1) turn down batch_window for affected cluster 2) enable temporary tenant rate limit 3) scale Dedicated pool or move tenant to fallback model. Who can execute change 1 now?
tom: I can patch batcher at the cluster level. Will push config: batch_window_ms: 10 and max_batch_tokens: 4096 to reduce tail formation. Pushing in 2m.
priya: I'll notify customer and ask them to hold retries while we mitigate. support-engineer: can you prepare a short reproduction script to validate after change?
support-engineer: got it. repro steps I'm drafting: curl loop with mixed long/short sequences, concurrent 200 reqs, headers include tenant-id: acme-inc. I'll share after the config change.
maya: adding runbook checklist: a) reduce batch window b) apply tenant throttling rule c) monitor dequeues and p99 d) if persists, fallback to smaller model + reserve extra capacity.
josh: Tom, do we have autopilot scaling capacity? I see Dedicated pools at 90% already.
tom: autoscaling triggered but cooldown prevented more nodes. I'll force one scale-up for hosted-us-east-batcher by manual override.
infra-bot: scale-up request accepted -> new instance provisioning started (instance id i-0abc1234) ETA ~4m
maya: after batcher config patch, watch for decrease in pending and p99. If not improving in 6m, enact tenant rate limit.
priya: customer notified: "We're investigating a request backlog causing timeouts. We're reducing batching latency and may temporarily throttle to stabilize. ETA 15-20m." they replied: "appreciate the quick response"
support-engineer: repro script (paste):
```
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "x-tenant-id: acme-inc" \
    -d '{"prompt":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1200}' &
done
wait
```
Run this from two clients to simulate burst.
josh: Tom, any change from the patch?
tom: patch applied. batch_window_ms -> 10ms, max_batch_tokens -> 4096. Observed immediate decrease in avg batch size from 14 -> 7. pending dropped from 18k -> 6k in ~90s.
maya: good. p95/p99 starting to drop. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/queue?s=now-15m
ops-oncall: still seeing tail >3s on some hosts. Recommend tenant rate limit to 30req/s while we continue to drain.
priya: applied temp rate-limit rule for acme-inc -> 30rps. Customer notified of a short throttle window.
support-engineer: reran repro locally after changes — fewer 502s, p50 improved. Still seeing occasional 504 when KV cache miss spikes.
josh: KV cache evictions remain high. Could we warm cache for that tenant or prioritize their KV entries? That might be heavy.
tom: warming is risky. Alternative: route acme-inc to a fallback model variant with shorter latency (quantized smaller model) until steady state.
maya: agree. Requesting model routing change for acme-inc to small-quantized-v1 for the next 45m. @eng-runtime FYI.
infra-bot: routing change request queued -> id route-87321. Deployment to gateway nodes started.
josh: with rate-limit + batcher change + routing fallback we should see improvement. Keep monitoring for 30m then reassess.
priya: customer update: "Thanks, saw latency improve. We'll pause heavy batch jobs for 1h." they want postmortem and action items.
support-engineer: documenting repro and metrics snapshot. Will attach to CS-9241.
maya: postmortem action items: 1) Add automatic tenant throttling heuristic when queue_pending > 10k 2) Add playbook step to reduce batch_window on high longseq traffic 3) Investigate KV cache prioritization 4) Improve autoscale cooldown logic for batchers
ops-oncall: assigning follow-up tasks: @tom for autoscale cooldown, @josh for throttling heuristic, @support-engineer for customer writeup.
josh: I'll start a ticket on the throttling heuristic and include simulation tests.
tom: I'll open infra PR to reduce cooldown and allow one emergency scale during pending>threshold.
priya: closing loop with customer, promised postmortem within 48h.
maya: final check: last 10m p99 down to ~1.2s and 5xx rate dropped to baseline. We'll leave routing fallback for 30m and then revert if stable.
priya: thanks all. marking incident as mitigated; continuing postmortem.
ops-oncall: incident -> mitigated. created postmortem draft at https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INC/6212345678
maya: nice work everyone :thumbsup:"
